subject: good citizen - delete output$XYZ when I know I won't need it again?

messages.author: c8fe4075ec631c03
messages.subject: good citizen - delete output$XYZ when I know I won't need it again?
parts:
I have a shiny app which generates a plot for every csv file it finds in a directory, and adds and removes plots as files come and go.

For each new file it rebuilds the htmlOutput to have another plotOutput with a name like "dynamic_plot_"+filename

For each new file it also pushes a renderPlot function into output, giving it a reactiveFileReader so it can update itself.

something like (pseudocode)

output[["dynamic_plot_"+filename]] <- plotFn(filename, reactiveFileReader(filename,...))

When a file gets deleted, the reactiveFileReader fires and asks the plot to regenerate, which then finds the file is missing.

At this point the output$dynamic_plot_one.csv is no longer (and never again) needed - so should I delete it?

If so, how, if not, does it and it's cached versions stick around forever in the R session?

-Alex
